records.topic: Set-universe closure: naturals, subsets, powersets, indexed unions
records.mathematics: A set-universe U contains ℕ, contains every subset of each of its members, contains the power set of each member, and contains ⋃ᵢ Aᵢ whenever I ∈ U and Aᵢ ∈ U for every i ∈ I.
records.proof: This is a definition. Existence of such universes is a separate assumption.
records.plain: A universe is a collection of sets closed under the operations the notes will use. Subset closure and power-set closure are different conditions: one includes each subset, the other includes the set of all subsets.
records.story: Mira keeps a library of sets. Its charter admits the natural numbers, every subcollection of a catalogued set, a catalogue of all those subcollections, and unions of catalogued families whose index set is also catalogued.
records.limit: The library is a set of sets with exact closure conditions, not an actual physical collection. The charter does not prove that a library satisfying it exists.

records.topic: Russell argument: a universe is not its own member
records.mathematics: If U is closed under subsets of its members, then U ∉ U. Under U ∈ U the separation set R = {A ∈ U | A ∉ A} is a member of U; its defining condition at R yields R ∈ R ↔ R ∉ R.
records.proof: Assume U ∈ U. Subset closure gives R ∈ U. Substitute R into the separation condition and derive a contradiction. Only subset closure is used in this argument.
records.plain: The contradiction concerns a set that would contain itself while supporting this separation construction. It is not a ban on talking about collections from a larger universe.
records.story: Mira supposes the whole library is itself a listed book. She forms the subcatalogue of listed books that do not list themselves. The charter makes that subcatalogue a listed book too. Asking whether it lists itself forces both answers to contradict their defining rule.
records.limit: Self-listing represents membership, not ordinary book citation. The argument needs a precise separation set and closure hypothesis.

records.topic: Three nested set-universes and membership assumptions
records.mathematics: Assume three set-universes Uₛ ⊆ Uₗ ⊆ Uₕ, together with Uₛ ∈ Uₗ and Uₗ ∈ Uₕ. Inclusion and membership are distinct relations.
records.proof: The source adopts these conditions as a convention; it does not derive universe existence.
records.plain: The notes reserve three size levels. The larger collection contains every member of the smaller one and also contains that smaller collection as a single set.
records.story: Mira has a small library, a larger library and an archive. Each next collection includes the earlier books and also catalogues the entire earlier library as one object.
records.limit: Lean's type-universe hierarchy is not itself this set-membership statement. A faithful set-theoretic encoding must keep the existence assumptions explicit.

records.topic: Small, large and huge sets
records.mathematics: Relative to the three assumed universes, small sets are members of Uₛ, large sets are members of Uₗ, and huge sets are members of Uₕ.
records.proof: Terminology defined by membership; the inclusions imply small ⇒ large ⇒ huge.
records.plain: Size is relative to the fixed universes. It is a membership classification, not a claim that a small set has few elements.
records.story: Mira labels a set by the catalogues admitting it. A book in the small catalogue also appears in the larger ones, even if it describes infinitely many things.
records.limit: The labels are mathematical universe membership, not numerical bounds or memory limits.

records.topic: Objects, hom sets, identities, typed composition, unit and associativity laws
records.mathematics: A strict category has objects, a hom set C(x,y) for each pair, identities 1ₓ and typed composition. For f:x→y, g:y→z, h:z→t, f∘1ₓ=f, 1ᵧ∘f=f, and (h∘g)∘f=h∘(g∘f). Object and hom sets satisfy the source's large-set bounds.
records.proof: The laws are part of the category structure, not propositions about every arbitrary graph.
records.plain: Giving arrows alone is insufficient: composition and identities must be specified and must obey the laws.
records.story: Mira's route book supplies a neutral permit at each town and a combined permit for every composable pair. Regrouping a chain must produce the same entry.
records.limit: Arrows need not be functions or journeys. Mathlib categories use type universes; the set-universe existence assumptions remain separate.

records.topic: Small versus locally small categories
records.mathematics: A strict category is locally small if each hom set is small. It is small if it is locally small and its object set is small.

records.plain: Local smallness bounds the arrows between a fixed pair. It says nothing by itself about the size of the whole collection of objects.

records.limit: Here small means relative universe size, not finite.

records.limit: The analogy does not prove closure or the non-smallness claims. These require separate mathematical checks.

records.topic: Isomorphism, inverse and isomorphic objects
records.mathematics: An arrow f:x→y is invertible if there exists g:y→x with g∘f=1ₓ and f∘g=1ᵧ. Objects are isomorphic if such an arrow exists.

records.limit: An isomorphism need not be equality of objects. One certified round trip is insufficient.

records.topic: Bijections, pointed bijections, linear bijections and homeomorphisms
records.mathematics: Isomorphisms in Set are bijections; in pointed Set they are point-preserving bijections; in Vectₖ they are bijective linear maps; in Top they are homeomorphisms.
records.proof: Two inverse morphisms give inverse functions. Conversely, the inverse of a bijection preserves the point or linear structure when the forward map does. For topology, inverse continuity is required and is part of a homeomorphism.
records.plain: Bijectivity alone works for the first three examples with their stated structures. A continuous bijection alone need not be a topological isomorphism.
records.story: Mira can reverse a transfer only if its return obeys the same book's rules. The continuous-transfer book explicitly checks the return's continuity too.
records.limit: The story is not a reason to infer inverse continuity. Each category needs its own equivalence between the two descriptions.

records.story: Mira either erases a book's special rules or equips an ordinary list with a new marked entry, a basis, or one of two extreme topologies. Every relabelling must extend consistently.
records.limit: These are seven distinct functors. Their adjunction properties are additional results in 3.2.

records.topic: What an infinity-category means informally
records.mathematics: An infinity-category is introduced informally through objects, arrows and higher arrows, with weakly coherent composition. This introductory description is not a complete formal definition.
records.proof: No proof-bearing formal definition is asserted in this introductory passage.
records.plain: The opening motivates a setting in which relations between maps are themselves part of the structure.
records.story: Mira's route book now records comparisons between permits and comparisons between those comparisons, without declaring a final formal charter.
records.limit: The picture is motivation. An ordinary Lean category does not encode the full higher structure.
records.formalization_status: Not proof-bearing; source definition or motivation without a supplied formal higher model

records.topic: Objects, arrows, higher parallel morphisms
records.mathematics: The introductory hierarchy consists of objects, morphisms between objects, 2-morphisms between parallel morphisms, and higher morphisms between parallel morphisms of the preceding dimension.
records.proof: This is an informal description of dimensions, not a completed axiom system.
records.plain: At each level, comparisons have endpoints at the previous level.
records.story: Mira compares two permits with the same endpoints, then compares two such comparisons, and continues the ledger to higher levels.
records.limit: No finite tower of ordinary arrows is claimed to formalize all dimensions.
records.formalization_status: Not proof-bearing; source definition or motivation without a supplied formal higher model

records.topic: Weak invertibility above dimension one; coherent unit/associativity
records.mathematics: In the intended infinity-category setting, k-morphisms for k≥2 are invertible in a weak sense, and units and associativity hold through compatible higher identifications.
records.proof: The exact weak structures and their axioms are deferred in the source.
records.plain: Higher identifications replace some strict equations, but those identifications must themselves fit together.
records.story: Mira allows regrouping certificates rather than identical route entries, and then requires certificates comparing the different ways of using those certificates.
records.limit: Lean's proof-irrelevant equality does not provide the intended higher identity structure; no ordinary analogue is a proof of this synthetic claim.

records.topic: Paths and homotopies fixing endpoints/boundaries
records.mathematics: For a topological space, points, paths, endpoint-fixing homotopies and higher boundary-fixing homotopies motivate the fundamental infinity-groupoid. Path concatenation is associative and unital up to homotopy; reversal is an inverse up to homotopy.
records.proof: The source sketches the construction. The one-dimensional homotopy laws have ordinary topological formalizations; the full infinite construction requires a precise higher model.
records.plain: Concatenating parameterized paths in different groupings changes the parameterization, but a homotopy relates the results.
records.story: Mira redraws journeys continuously while keeping the endpoints fixed. A journey out and back can be contracted, and different timing conventions can be deformed into one another.
records.limit: A homotopy is a specified continuous deformation. This does not make the parameterized paths literally equal or formalize all higher coherence.

records.topic: Indiscernibility, transport and Structure Identity Principle
records.mathematics: Equality allows substitution of properties and transport of structures. The intended structure identity principle relates identities of groups to group isomorphisms. Existence of an element of order two is isomorphism-invariant; presentation-specific statements about the identity being the number 0 need not be. The source compares the cyclic group on {0,1} with the multiplicative group {1,−1}.
records.proof: Equality transport is available in ordinary dependent type theory. Group isomorphisms preserve multiplication, the identity and element order. The structure identity principle requires the intended univalent/homotopical setting.
records.plain: Ordinary equality supports substitution. Isomorphism preserves structural properties, but not every statement about how a structure was represented as sets.
records.story: Two clerks encode the same two-state group with different labels. An element of order two survives translation, while the printed name of the identity can change. Mira distinguishes a change of labels from a change of group structure.
records.limit: Group isomorphism is not automatically equality of Lean's bundled groups. A proof of order invariance does not prove the structure identity principle.

records.topic: Equality, isomorphism and equivalence-sensitive invariance
records.mathematics: Equality, isomorphism and equivalence of strict categories are distinct notions. The one-object category and walking isomorphism are equivalent despite having different numbers of objects.
records.proof: The explicit functors and natural isomorphisms are given in items 3.8–3.9; the object sets have cardinalities one and two.
records.plain: Equivalence permits redundant isomorphic objects. A strict isomorphism of categories would require inverse object functions.
records.story: Mira's two-room ledger and one-room model have different numbers of names but equivalent permit structure.
records.limit: The distinction concerns object presentations and categorical equivalence, not equality of the chosen object sets.

records.topic: Every ordinary equivalence can be upgraded to an adjoint equivalence
records.mathematics: Every equivalence in the source's quasi-inverse sense can be promoted to an adjoint equivalence.
records.proof: The source cites this fact without using it. In ordinary category theory one can modify the unit or counit to obtain the triangle identities while retaining quasi-inverse functors.
records.plain: Arbitrary natural isomorphisms witnessing a quasi-inverse need not already satisfy the triangles. An upgrade supplies coherent choices.
records.story: Mira already has reversible round-trip comparisons. She adjusts the certificates so the two special triangle journeys agree with the neutral permits.
records.limit: Do not assume the original comparison isomorphisms already satisfy the triangle identities.
